issues.body:
The new block runs `"$BENCH_GEO" nearest-ids "$CORPUS" "$k" > "$TMP/sparq-$wl.ids"` as a bare simple command inside a for-loop. The script is `set -euo pipefail` (line 94), so this is NOT in a condition context and any nonzero exit terminates the script.

bench_geo's nearest-ids path can exit nonzero on several ordinary conditions: `std::process::exit(2)` on argument-parse failure, and `panic!` (exit 101) on `read corpus` or `parse corpus` failure. When that happens the harness dies immediately after the sparq timing leg has already SUCCEEDED — the jena leg never runs and step 3 never emits the envelope, so a complete, expensive sparq run is thrown away and the script exits nonzero.

This contradicts the contract stated in this same file's header: 'a timeout/error degrades to an honest ERROR row, never a number' and 'the script still exits 0'. Every other engine invocation in the script honours that (the run.sh leg at 219-226, the adapter at 261-263, the geographica legs at 539-544 are all `if ... ; then ... else record-ERROR ; fi`, and all are wrapped in `timeout`).

Secondly, unlike every other engine invocation here, this one has no `timeout` wrapper, so it is not covered by the documented per-workload wall-clock cap. It also loads and re-indexes the full 100k corpus twice (once per k), which is now added to the ONLY=sparq GEO_SMOKE acceptance path.
issues.fix_hint:
Guard it the same way as the other legs, and remove the stale output on failure so the envelope's fail-closed path is taken rather than the script dying:

  for spec in "nearest_k10 10" "nearest_k100 100"; do
    read -r wl k <<< "$spec"
    if ! timeout "$TIMEOUT_S" "$BENCH_GEO" nearest-ids "$CORPUS" "$k" > "$TMP/sparq-$wl.ids"; then
      log "sparq: $wl entity-ID oracle FAILED; timing will be withheld"
      rm -f "$TMP/sparq-$wl.ids"
    fi
  done

That mirrors the jena-side handling you already wrote at 275-296 and keeps read_ids() returning None -> ids_agree=False -> timing withheld, instead of aborting the run.
issues.title: sparq nearest-ids call is unguarded under `set -e` and uncapped: a failure aborts the whole run and discards a completed timing leg

issues.body:
The new sidecar calls `urllib.request.urlopen(request)` with no `timeout=` argument. Python's default is the global socket timeout, which is None, so this blocks forever. The `python3 - ...` invocation is also the only jena-facing call in the script that is NOT wrapped in `timeout "$TIMEOUT_S"` (contrast lines 261 and 580).

The file header documents 'per-workload wall-clock cap (TIMEOUT_S, covering the whole best-of-N series); a timeout/error degrades to an honest ERROR row, never a number'. This replay is an additional, uncapped query against the same endpoint executed after the timed series, so a fuseki instance that stops responding (GC pause, spatial-index thrash on nearest_k100, a half-closed socket) wedges the entire benchmark run with no cap and no diagnostic. The `if ! python3 ...` guard handles a failing exit but does nothing about a hang.

Note this is reachable in exactly the situation the oracle exists for — a large-k ORDER BY replay over a 100k-triple in-memory dataset.
issues.fix_hint: Do both: wrap the sidecar in the same per-workload cap used elsewhere (`if ! timeout "$TIMEOUT_S" python3 - "$ENDPOINT" ...`), and pass an explicit socket timeout in the Python itself, e.g. `with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=int(os.environ.get("TIMEOUT_S", "300"))) as response:` (exporting TIMEOUT_S into the sidecar's environment). The existing failure branch — log + `rm -f "$TMP/jena-$wl.ids"` — then correctly withholds the timing.
issues.title: jena entity-ID oracle replay has no timeout: an unresponsive endpoint hangs the harness indefinitely

issues.body:
The withheld string was relabelled from `count-disagree` to `result-disagree` but still interpolates only `s` and `j` (the counts):

    row["jena_geosparql_us"] = (
        "WITHHELD(result-disagree: sparq=%s jena=%s)" % (s, j)
    )

The headline case this PR is built for is precisely count_agree=True with entity_ids_agree=False — a degenerate ORDER BY returning the right NUMBER of wrong rows. In that case the envelope's timings block reads `WITHHELD(result-disagree: sparq=10 jena=10)`, i.e. it reports two identical values as the reason for a disagreement. A reader of the timings table cannot tell why the timing was withheld without cross-referencing count_crosscheck, and the surface reading is that the harness withheld a timing for no reason.

The underlying data is preserved in count_crosscheck (entity_ids_agree, sparq_entity_ids, jena_entity_ids), so nothing is lost — this is a reporting-clarity defect in the one string a reader of the envelope's timing table actually sees.
issues.fix_hint:
Distinguish the two failure modes in the reason, e.g.:

    if not count_agree:
        reason = "count-disagree: sparq=%s jena=%s" % (s, j)
    else:
        reason = "entity-set-disagree: counts=%s, |sparq\\jena|=%d |jena\\sparq|=%d" % (
            s, len(set(sparq_ids or []) - set(jena_ids or [])),
            len(set(jena_ids or []) - set(sparq_ids or [])))
    row["jena_geosparql_us"] = "WITHHELD(%s)" % reason

The symmetric-difference sizes make the degenerate-ORDER-BY case self-evident in the timings table.
issues.title: WITHHELD reason interpolates only counts, so an entity-set-only disagreement reads as a self-contradiction ("sparq=10 jena=10")

issues.body:
Both .rq headers were updated to say the harness now cross-checks the exact entity-IRI set, and both explicitly cite research/gap-geo-2026-07.md as the authority. That record was not updated and now contradicts them — §5, around line 140:

  "The only cross-checked value for these workloads is the result-set SIZE (== k on a corpus larger than k), never the ordering or the exact points returned."

It also still describes the pinned rendering as `ORDER BY ASC(geof:distance(...)) LIMIT k`, whereas the committed queries use `spatialF:greatCircleGeom` per the sq-a8anf correction. Section 3 ('INVARIANT: counts-not-coordinates', line ~83) likewise needs the nearest_k carve-out that the script header and the envelope note now carry.

The change direction is strictly a strengthening, so nothing shipped is overclaimed — but the record is the document the .rq files send a reader to, and it now understates the gate.

(bench/geo/README.md:40 does NOT need changing: it describes run.sh's expected.tsv gate, which really is counts-only.)
issues.fix_hint: Update research/gap-geo-2026-07.md §5 to state that nearest_k is now cross-checked as an exact entity-IRI SET via an untimed oracle replay on both sides (sparq: `bench_geo nearest-ids`; jena: a second SPARQL-JSON replay of the pinned query), that ordering and coordinates remain uncompared, and correct the rendering to spatialF:greatCircleGeom. Add the nearest_k carve-out to the §3 counts-not-coordinates invariant so it matches the script header and the envelope's count_crosscheck_note.
issues.title: The design record this header points at still says result-set SIZE is the only cross-checked value for nearest_k

issues.body:
`read_ids` returns `[]` (not None) for an existing-but-empty file, and `ids_agree = sparq_ids == jena_ids and sparq_ids is not None` evaluates `[] == []` to True. Nothing anywhere checks that the ID sets have k members.

Today this is hard to reach: the shell `>` redirect truncates the sparq file before the binary runs, but with the set -e abort (issue 1) an empty file never reaches the envelope, and jena's empty-bindings case is caught by count_agree. Once issue 1 is fixed with `rm -f`, the missing-file path is fail-closed too. So this is defence-in-depth rather than a live bug — but the entire premise of this PR is that an oracle which can be vacuously green is worthless, and this oracle has exactly one such degenerate state left.

Related: both sides collapse to a `set` (the sidecar's `{row["e"]["value"] for row in bindings}` and read_ids' `sorted(set(...))`), so multiplicity is discarded. Harmless on this corpus (one asWKT per entity) but it means a duplicate-row bug on either side would be silently absorbed rather than surfaced.
issues.fix_hint: Thread the expected k through and assert it, e.g. record `{"nearest_k10": 10, "nearest_k100": 100}` (or parse the trailing digits of the workload name) and require `len(sparq_ids) == len(jena_ids) == k` as part of ids_agree, exposing a `expected_k` field in the crosscheck. Optionally compare sorted lists rather than sorted sets so a duplicate-row regression shows up as a disagreement instead of being deduped away.
issues.title: Oracle never asserts cardinality, so two empty ID sets compare as agreement

issues.body:
Line 4 still opens 'Two modes:' while the fenced block below it now lists three invocations, and the per-mode headings run '## Mode 2 contract' then '## Mode 4 — query' with no '## Mode 3' section — the new nearest-ids mode is documented only as a bullet in the usage block. (The binary in fact dispatches five: gen, bench, nearest-ids, query, and the default report mode.)

I checked for dangling references to the old numbering elsewhere in the repo and found none, so this is contained to this file's header.
issues.fix_hint: Change 'Two modes:' to something count-free ('Modes:'), and either give nearest-ids its own '## Mode 3 — nearest-ids <corpus.nt> <k>' heading describing the untimed-oracle contract and the fact that it replays the same index.nearest(QUERY_CENTER, k) call bench mode times, or drop the ordinal numbering entirely and name the sections after the subcommands.
issues.title: Module doc mode numbering is now inconsistent: "Two modes" with three listed, and no Mode 3 heading

verdict.summary:
The core idea is sound and a genuine strengthening: nearest_k previously passed on a size-only (==k) check that stayed vacuously green while jena's ORDER BY had degenerated to the ?e tie-break (sq-a8anf). Comparing the exact entity-IRI set fixes that. I verified the load-bearing details: GeoIndex::nearest returns Vec<(&Term, f64)> and oxrdf Term Display emits <iri> (per assertions at crates/sparq-canon/src/lib.rs:599), matching the sidecar's "<%s>" rendering, so the two sides are format-compatible; nearest_ids_mode replays the SAME index.nearest(QUERY_CENTER, k) call bench_mode times, so the oracle is not measuring a different path; k=10/100 matches LIMIT 10/100 in the pinned .rq files; and both engines are great-circle on the same mean sphere, so the k-set ranking is invariant to any radius-scale difference. The envelope logic is fail-closed: a missing/failed jena oracle file gives ids_agree=False and withholds the timing.

What blocks approval is harness wiring, not oracle semantics. The script runs under `set -euo pipefail`, and every other engine invocation is either guarded by an if/else that records an honest ERROR row or wrapped in `timeout`. Neither new invocation follows that: the sparq `nearest-ids` call is a bare command in a for-loop, so any nonzero exit (arg-parse exit 2, corpus read/parse panic) aborts the whole run, discarding an already-completed sparq timing leg and emitting no envelope — contradicting this file's documented graceful-degradation/exit-0 contract. The jena replay uses urlopen with no timeout and no `timeout` wrapper, so a wedged endpoint hangs the harness past the documented per-workload cap.

Also: the WITHHELD string still interpolates only counts, so an entity-set-only disagreement prints as "sparq=10 jena=10"; and research/gap-geo-2026-07.md still says size is the only cross-checked value here, which the updated .rq headers now contradict while citing that record.
